user: And I still have time to file, right?
answer:
Whether you still have time depends on the reason code, because each code has its own window counted from the transaction date (2026-07-20). Based on today's date of 2026-09-15 from your limit data:

- **unauthorized_debit (56 days):** Closed. The window ended around 2026-09-14, so this code can no longer be used for TX-0401.
- **duplicate_charge (60 days):** Open, but closing soon. The window ends around 2026-09-18.
- **goods_not_received (90 days), service_not_rendered (90 days), fraud_card_not_present (120 days):** Open, with more time remaining.

Eligibility is still confirmed only when I run the check, and eligibility also depends on the transaction's status and any account-level restrictions. If you believe duplicate_charge applies, that is the most time-sensitive option. Tell me which code fits and I'll run the check.

Payment dispute rules
## Reason codes and chargeback windows
Each reason code has a window in days from the transaction date. A dispute opened after the window closes is not eligible.

| Reason code | Window (days) |
|---|---|
| fraud_card_not_present | 120 |
| goods_not_received | 90 |
| duplicate_charge | 60 |
| service_not_rendered | 90 |
| unauthorized_debit | 56 |

Dispute handling process
## Withdrawing a dispute
A customer may withdraw a dispute at any time before resolution. Withdrawal is
final; the same transaction cannot be disputed again under the same reason code.

Glossary
## Chargeback window
The number of days, counted from the transaction date, during which a dispute
may be raised under a given reason code.

Limit operations
## Window definition
Limits are tracked on calendar days, not business days. The daily window runs
from 00:00 to 23:59 CET.
